create.name: Sister Jenna
create.bio:
Sister Jenna is a meditation teacher in the Brahma Kumaris tradition, the Raja Yoga movement that began in India, and leads its work in the Washington, D.C. area. She founded the Brahma Kumaris Meditation Museum, with centres in Maryland and Virginia, and she has travelled to more than ninety countries to teach. An honorary doctorate from St. Thomas Aquinas College recognised her years of service, and she is also known as Sister Dr. Jenna.

She hosts the America Meditating radio show and its video channel, where she talks with authors, scientists, entrepreneurs and spiritual teachers, and has led regular guided meditations there on themes such as letting go, peace of mind and inner power. She has hosted online summits, including one for The Shift Network, and runs civic projects such as Meditate the Vote and Pause for Peace that invite people to bring calm reflection into public life. Her written work includes a book of meditations published by Sacred Stories and a memoir about her mother, Sister Gita, and she has released several albums of guided meditation commentary.

books.title: Meditation: Intimate Experiences with the Divine through Contemplative Practices
books.author: Sister Dr. Jenna
books.description: A book of meditations and short reflections from Sister Jenna, drawn from her Raja Yoga practice, for building a daily habit of turning inwards. Published by Sacred Stories in 2022.

courses.title: Guided Meditation Albums by Sister Jenna
courses.description: Downloadable albums of her guided meditation commentaries, including Your Inner World, Off The Grid, Off To Work and Inclusion Revolution. Each album is a set of spoken reflections for quiet practice at home or at work.

free_resources.title: Seven-Day Meditations with Sister Jenna
free_resources.description: A free series of short guided meditation commentaries, one for each day of a week, on themes such as belief and benevolence. The page also introduces what meditation is in the Raja Yoga approach.
